---
title: Documentation
description: A native macOS video editor. Cut, grade, caption, animate and export it yourself, or ask the Assistant or any MCP agent to do it.
eyebrow: Documentation
template: splash
editUrl: false
hero:
  # Distinct from `title` above, so the browser tab reads "Documentation | Frame Job" while the
  # hero opens with the product's name.
  title: Frame Job
  tagline: A native macOS video editor. Cut it yourself, ask the Assistant, or let any MCP agent drive. Every edit is an ordinary undo step.
  image:
    file: ../../assets/logo.svg
    alt: The Frame Job mark, a frame and a playhead inside a viewfinder's four corners
  actions:
    - text: Get started
      link: /getting-started/requirements-and-install/
      variant: primary
      icon: right-arrow
    - text: All features
      link: /features/
      variant: secondary
    - text: Download
      link: https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/FrameJob.dmg
      variant: minimal
      icon: external
---

import { Card, CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

<Shot
  name="04-editor.window"
  alt="The Frame Job editor window: a preview above a timeline with music, shape, graphic and title tracks, and an inspector down the right."
/>

Frame Job runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 26 or later. There's no account to make. Every AI feature runs on your own API key, and everything else works without one.

## Start here

<CardGrid>
  <LinkCard
    title="Your first edit"
    description="Open a movie, cut it, and export it."
    href="/getting-started/first-edit/"
  />
  <LinkCard
    title="A tour of the editor window"
    description="What each part of the window is for."
    href="/getting-started/editor-window/"
  />
  <LinkCard
    title="Core concepts"
    description="Projects, tracks, clips and the canvas."
    href="/getting-started/core-concepts/"
  />
  <LinkCard
    title="AI features and your own keys"
    description="What's optional, and what stays on your Mac."
    href="/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/"
  />
</CardGrid>

## What you can do

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Cut" icon="seti:video">
    [Trim](/editing/trimming/), [slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/),
    [split](/editing/splitting/) and [nest](/editing/nests/) clips on tracks that hold anything.
    Take out dead air with [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and
    [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/), or
    [cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/) from the transcript.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Compose" icon="seti:image">
    Place [text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) and
    [pictures](/text-and-shapes/image-clips/) on a fixed canvas, use
    [matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/), and
    [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) with no green screen.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Animate" icon="rocket">
    Ease any property with [actions](/motion/actions/), use
    [motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) and [transitions](/motion/transitions/), build
    [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/), and drop in [motion graphics](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Grade" icon="seti:favicon">
    [Wheels](/color/wheels/), [curves](/color/curves/), [looks](/color/looks/),
    [LUTs](/color/luts/), [qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) and
    [scopes](/color/scopes/), with [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/) and
    [HDR projects](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Mix" icon="seti:audio">
    [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [EQ](/audio/eq/),
    [ducking](/audio/ducking/), [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) to a loudness target, and
    [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) across cameras and recorders.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Caption" icon="comment-alt">
    [Generate captions](/captions/generate-captions/) on your Mac or with AssemblyAI, as
    [subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) or [word-by-word styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/),
    and read your project as [a transcript](/captions/transcript-tab/).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Record" icon="laptop">
    Record [a display](/recording/record-a-display/) or
    [a window](/recording/record-a-window/) with [a camera beside it](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/),
    then [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/) and
    [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Reframe" icon="seti:crystal">
    [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) keeps a person in frame, and
    [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) turns a whole edit into 9:16, 4:5 or
    1:1. [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) cuts between cameras for you.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Deliver" icon="seti:config">
    [H.264 and HEVC](/export/h264-and-hevc/), [ProRes](/export/prores/),
    [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/), [transparent exports](/export/transparency/),
    [stems](/export/stems/) and an [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) that runs behind the editor.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## Work with an AI

input.command:
cd /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-ai-docs-int/docs/site && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='README.md'
s=open(p).read()
i=s.index('## Theme')
j=s.index('Every page may set an `eyebrow`')
new='''## Theme

The site wears the **Boppa Llewyn** design system, the one the company website and every app's
documentation share, so this site and Doctored's (`public-docs/` in the Doctored repository) look
like one family: Geist for text and Geist Mono for eyebrows, code, keys and versions, with no serif
anywhere; neutral greys with the logo green as the one accent; 6, 10 and 16 px corners; hairlines
between things, and shadows only on cards and the screenshot window. The header carries the
company mark, three toy blocks, with **Boppa Llewyn / Frame Job** after it.

The light look is **Neutral Light** and the dark look **Neutral Dark**, the pair the design system
recommends. `tokens.css` also carries its three alternate palettes (Cream & Coral, Field Green,
Monochrome) for comparison; nothing switches to them. Changing the palette means changing its two
look blocks in `tokens.css` and nothing else.

| Where | What |
| :---- | :--- |
| `src/styles/tokens.css` | The design system's `--bl-*` tokens (colour, shadow, spacing, radius, font), copied whole from the design handoff: Neutral Light under `[data-theme='light']`, Neutral Dark under `[data-theme='dark']`, the alternates at the end. Copy a new version in whole rather than editing a value. |
| `src/styles/boppa-llewyn.css` | The theme, shared rule for rule with Doctored's `custom.css` (only Prettier's formatting differs): the tokens mapped onto Starlight's `--sl-*` properties, then the parts the properties cannot reach. Change it in both sites together. |
| `src/styles/frame-job.css` | This site's own components (`Shot`, `AtAGlance`, the feature index) drawn with the tokens. |
| `src/fonts/font-face.css` | `@font-face` rules for Geist and Geist Mono, split by `unicode-range`. |
| `public/fonts/` | Self-hosted variable WOFF2 (the `latin` and `latin-ext` subsets from Google Fonts). Licence: `public/fonts/OFL.txt`. |
| `src/assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` | The company mark in the header. `src/assets/logo.svg`, the Frame Job mark, is the splash's hero image, and `public/favicon.svg` stays the Frame Job icon. |
| `src/components/` | The four Starlight overrides: `SiteTitle` (the mark, **Boppa Llewyn /**, the product's name and a version badge), `ThemeSelect` (a two-state toggle), `PageTitle` (the eyebrow and the description), `Hero` (the eyebrow). |
| `src/site.ts` | The badge's version, read from the repository's `VERSION` file when the site is built. |

`Shot` takes `frame` for a full-window capture (a `*.window` screen): the splash's editor window
is drawn in a window frame with a title bar. Partial captures (sheets, inspectors) stay unframed.

'''
s=s[:i]+new+s[j:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
pnpm exec prettier --write README.md src/styles src/fonts src/components astro.config.mjs > /dev/null; git diff --stat; sed -n '/## Theme/,/## Publishing/p' README.md | head -50

` is hidden and `.link-title` is made a block, giving the 2 px label-to-title gap. - **Feature index count:** mono 12 px `--bl-ink-subtle` with no uppercase (README wording).
